NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the critical intersection of advanced semiconductor design and AI infrastructure, acting as a fabless designer that is existentially dependent on TSMC's leading-edge nodes and a small set of HBM memory suppliers for its flagship AI accelerators. On the demand side, NVIDIA enjoys extraordinary leverage over hyperscale cloud providers (Microsoft, Meta, Google, Amazon) who are in an AI infrastructure arms race, making NVIDIA's H100/H200/Blackwell GPUs effectively mission-critical procurement for the world's largest technology companies.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the center of a highly concentrated hardware supply chain, relying on a small number of critical Asian semiconductor and display manufacturers — particularly TSMC and Samsung — to produce its proprietary silicon and key components. On the downstream side, Apple's products and Services ecosystem are distributed through major telecom carriers and global retailers, while its high-margin Services segment is deeply tied to platform relationships with large digital companies like Alphabet and Meta.

TSM.supply_chain_summary: TSMC sits at the critical center of the global semiconductor supply chain as the world's dominant pure-play foundry, translating cutting-edge equipment and materials from a handful of specialized suppliers into finished wafers for virtually every major fabless chip designer. Its position is uniquely irreplaceable in the near term, as advanced nodes below 7nm are almost exclusively produced by TSMC, making it an existential dependency for the AI, smartphone, and high-performance computing industries.

MU.supply_chain_summary: Micron Technology sits in the middle of the semiconductor value chain as a vertically integrated manufacturer of DRAM and NAND flash memory, heavily dependent on a small number of specialized equipment suppliers — particularly ASML, Lam Research, and Applied Materials — for its leading-edge fabrication capabilities. Its downstream customer base spans hyperscale cloud providers, AI accelerator vendors, mobile OEMs, and PC/server manufacturers, with growing criticality tied to HBM demand from AI GPU customers like NVIDIA.
